{"text": "My name is Mrs. Akinleye. For about the past two months, I have noticed that my husband's breathing has not been normal at all. He also sneezes repeatedly, especially whenever he is in a dusty environment or in a place where something is being fried. He sneezes repeatedly and finds it difficult to breathe properly.

His breathing becomes laboured, and he tends to sneeze whenever he is in places with smoke or dust.

Is there any test that can be carried out to determine exactly what is causing these symptoms? Could staying in dusty places be the cause, or is his body's system changing in a way that is making this happen? What type of medication can he use so that his breathing will become normal and comfortable at all times, wherever he may be?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Orúkọ mi ni Ìyá Àfín Akinlẹ́yẹ, láti bí oṣù méjì sẹ́yìn ni mo ti ṣàkíyèsí pé mímí ọkọ mi kò dára rárá. Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni ó sì máa ń sìn léraléra, pàápàá jùlọ tí ó bá ti wà ní ibì tí erùkù bá wà, tàbí ibi tí a ti ń din nǹkan. Yóò máa sìn léraléra, kò ní lè mí dé òkè, dé ilé.
Mímí ń rẹ̀ yóò máa ṣe jùlẹ̀jùlẹ̀, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni yóò sì máa sìn nígbàkúgbà tí ó bá wà ní ibì tí èéfín tàbí erùkù bá wà.
Njẹ́ àyẹ̀wò kan wà tí a lè ṣe, tí a lè fi mọ ohun pàtó tí ó fa irúfẹ́ nǹkan wọ̀nyí? Àbí dídúró níbi tí erùkù wà rẹ̀ ni ó fa èyí ni tàbí àgọ́ ara rẹ̀ ni ó ń yí padà tí irú èyí fi ń ṣẹlẹ̀? Irú òògùn wo ni ó lè lò tí mímí rẹ̀ yóò fi máa já gẹ́rẹ́gẹ́ ní gbogbo ìgbà àti ní òrékóre, ní ibikíbi tí ó bá wà?", "translated_text_language": "Yoruba", "audio_language": "Yoruba", "text_was_edited": false}

{"text": "A mother living in our neighborhood was pregnant with her second child. At the beginning of the pregnancy, everything was going normally, and she was happy that a new baby was coming. However, a few months ago, she began to experience severe lower abdominal pain. One day, the pain became so intense that she could hardly stand up properly. Shortly afterward, she also started having heavy vaginal bleeding. The bleeding was more than usual, and it made her very weak. When she saw the bleeding, she became frightened that her unborn baby might be in danger. Her husband quickly assisted her to go to the hospital.
My question is: what can cause severe lower abdominal pain during pregnancy? Is heavy bleeding during pregnancy a danger sign for the mother or the unborn baby?
What are the signs that indicate the pregnancy may be in trouble? Is there any medication that can stop the pain and bleeding without harming the unborn baby?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Ìyá ọmọ kan tó ń gbé ní ẹ̀gbẹ́ ilé wa ni ó lóyún ọmọ rẹ̀ kejì. Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ oyún náà, gbogbo nǹkan ń lọ dédé, inú rẹ̀ sì dùn pé, ọmọ tuntun ń bọ̀. Ṣùgbọ́n ní oṣù díẹ̀ sẹ́yìn, ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní ní ìrora tó lágbára ní ìsàlẹ̀ inú. Ní ọjọ́ kan, ìrora náà pọ̀ tó bẹ́ẹ̀ tí kò lè fi dìde dáadáa. Kò pé, ó tún bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní rí ẹ̀jẹ̀ púpọ̀, tó ń yọ lára rẹ̀. Ẹ̀jẹ̀ náà ju bíi. Ẹ̀jẹ̀ yìí pọ̀ ju bí ó ṣe máa ń rí lọ, ó sì máa ń mú kó rẹ̀ gan. Bí ó ṣe rí ẹ̀jẹ̀ yìí, ẹ̀rù bà á pé bóyá ọmọ inú rẹ̀ wà nínú ewu. Ní kíákíá ni ọkọ rẹ̀ ràn án lọ́wọ́ láti lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn.
Ìbéèrè mi ni kí ni ó lè fa ìrora tó lágbára ní ìsàlẹ̀ inú nígbà oyún? Ṣé ẹ̀jẹ̀ púpọ̀ tó ń yọ nígbà oyún jẹ́ àmì ewu fún ìyá tàbí ọmọ inú rẹ̀?
Kí ni àwọn àfihàn tó fi hàn pé oyún náà wà nínú ìṣòro? Ṣé òògùn wà tó lè da ìrora àti ẹ̀jẹ̀ dúró, láì ba ọmọ inú rẹ̀ jẹ?", "translated_text_language": "Yoruba", "audio_language": "Yoruba", "text_was_edited": false}

{"text": "I am an married woman, thirty-five years old. Please, I brought my five-month-old baby for examination and guidance.
I have resumed work. But surprisingly, for about the past three days, I have noticed that my baby has been coughing repeatedly. We have tried everything we can think of to stop the cough, but I can see that the cough has not gone away.
I am usually not at home. When I leave in the morning, I do not return until around 6 p.m. My mother stays at home with the baby.
Whenever I have the opportunity to call, I do so and ask about the cough, and they keep telling me that the baby is still coughing.
The baby is five months old. He is no longer taking only breast milk because I have resumed work. I breastfed him exclusively for three months, and after that I started giving him other foods.
I have been giving him different foods, including pap, and other baby foods that I know.
What is even more surprising is that since last night, his breathing has not been normal. He is not breathing well, and his nose is completely blocked.
My mother even said that while bathing him this morning, she had to use a little warm water around his nose and chest because the cough had become severe.
The breathing problem has also started. He is no longer breathing properly, and his breathing is not clear and free anymore.
Please, my question is: what can I use for him to stop the cough? And concerning the breathing that is no longer clear, what can I do, what can I use for him, and what steps can I take so that he can breathe properly and nothing will obstruct his breathing?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Mo jẹ ọmọbìnrin àbílékọ ọdún márùn-ún dín lógójì. Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, ọmọ mi, ọmọ oṣù márùn-ún yìí ni mo gbé wá fún àyẹ̀wò àti fún ìtọ́ni.
Mo ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ iṣẹ́ padà. Ṣùgbọ́n sí ìyàlẹ́nu ni bí àti bí ọjọ́ mẹ́ta báyìí mo rí pé ọmọ mi ṣá ń wúkọ lémọ lémọ lémọ. Gbogbo ìgbìyànjú, gbogbo ohun tí a lè ṣe ni a ti gbìyànjú láti ṣe fún láti dá ikọ́ náà dúró. Ṣùgbọ́n mo rí pé ikọ́ náà ò tíì lọ.
Èmi ò dé kì í sí nílé. Tí mo bá ti lọ láàárọ̀, ó di ìrólé bí aago mẹ́fà kí n tó padà sílé. Màmá mi ni ọmọ náà máa ń wà pẹ̀lú nílé.
Àmọ́ nígbà tí mo bá ní ànfààní láti pè, mo máa ń pè, tí mo sì máa ń béèrè pé báwo ni ikọ́ náà, tí wọ́n á dé sọ fún mi pé ó ṣì ń wú ikọ́ náà.
Ọmọ oṣù márùn-ún ni ọmọ náà. Omu nìkan kò lò ń mu, torí mo ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ iṣẹ́. Mo fún un ní omu nìkan fún oṣù mẹ́ta, lẹ́yìn ìgbà yẹn mo ti ń fún ní àwọn oúnjẹ.
Mo ti ń fún ní àwọn oúnjẹ, mo ń fún ní ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀, mo dé ń fún ní àwọn oúnjẹ ọmọde tí mo mọ̀.
Ìyàlẹ́nu tó tún wà ni pé láti bí alẹ́ àná, mímí rẹ̀ ò wà já gàrà mọ́. Kò mí dáadáa, gbogbo imú rẹ̀ ti di.
Màmá mi gan-an nígbà tí wọ́n wẹ láàárọ̀ yìí, wọ́n ní láti fi omi tó lọ́wọ́rọ̀ díẹ̀ láti jó ní ní imú, jó ní ìgbàyà, torí ikọ́ yẹn pọ̀.
Èémí yẹn náà dé tún ti wá bẹ̀rẹ̀, kò mí dáadáa mọ́, èémí yẹn ò já gàrà mọ́.
Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, ìbéèrè mi ni pé, kí ni mo lè lò fún láti dáwọ́ ikọ́ náà dúró, kí ikọ́ náà lè dúró? Àti pé èémí tí ò wà já gàrà, kí ni mo lè ṣe, kí ni mo lè lò fún un, ìgbésẹ̀ wo ni mo lè gbé tó máa fi máa mí, tí ohunkóhun o ní di lọ́wọ́ láti mí?", "translated_text_language": "Yoruba", "audio_language": "Yoruba", "text_was_edited": false}

{"text": "A woman just gave birth to a newborn baby at our hospital this morning. Her delivery was very easy, and she gave birth to the baby smoothly and without complications.
Shortly after this woman gave birth, we observed that the pad placed under her quickly became soaked with blood, and it was quite a lot. A few minutes later, the woman used another pad, yet it was also filled with blood, very quickly. Before long, the woman started feeling weak, and the bleeding became so heavy that it did not stop.
What could be the cause of postpartum hemorrhage? What could cause the bleeding to not stop? Is it possible that a second baby remains inside this woman? Is it possible that the woman's cervix is torn? Is it possible that her uterus is failing to contract to stop the bleeding? What could cause the heavy, continuous bleeding this woman is experiencing? What steps can we take for this woman to stop the bleeding? What kind of injection or medication can be used for this woman, and should we send this woman to a larger hospital, or is there another procedure we can perform on this woman to make the bleeding stop?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Arabinrin kan lo be ọmọ tuntun jojolo si ile iwosan wa ni aaro  yii. Lẹ́yìn ìṣẹ́jú kàtí-kán ti arábìnrin yìí bí ọmọ, paàdì tí a fi sí ìdí rẹ̀, a rí pé kò pẹ̀ rárá tí ẹjẹ́ fìkún inú paàdì náà, tí ó sì pọ̀ púpọ̀. Lẹ́yìn ìṣẹ́jú kejì ẹ̀wẹ́, arábìnrin yìí tún lò paàdì mìíràn, síbẹ̀ òun náà kún fún ẹ̀jẹ̀, ní kiakia. Láìpẹ̀, láìjínà, arábìnrin bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní bí wípé o rẹ ọ̀ún, ẹ jẹ̀ náà wá pọ̀ dé ibi pé ẹ̀jẹ̀ náà kò dá.
Kí ló ṣeṣe, kí ó fa ẹ̀jẹ̀ lẹ́yìn ìbímọ? Kí ló ṣeṣe, kí ó fa, tí ẹ̀jẹ̀ náà kò fìdúró? Ǹjẹ́ ó ṣeṣe, kí ìkejì ọmọ kó kù nínú arábìnrin yìí? Ǹjẹ́ ó ṣeṣe, kí ẹnu ilé ọmọ arábìnrin ko yà bí? Kí ni àwọn ohun tí a le ṣe fún arábìnrin, láti jẹ́ kí ẹ̀jẹ̀ náà kò dáwọ́ dúró? Irú abẹrẹ tàbí ògùn wo ni a le lò fún arábìnrin yìí, ǹjẹ́ kí a jẹ́ kí arábìnrin yìí kí ó ma lọ sí ilé-ìwé sọ, aláàdànláà náà ni, àbí o ńkò ọ̀kan wà, tí a tún le ṣe fún arábìnrin yìí, láti jẹ́ kí ẹ̀jẹ̀ náà kò mọwọ́ dúró?
", "translated_text_language": "Yoruba", "audio_language": "Yoruba", "text_was_edited": false}

{"text": "Suddenly, we saw one of our pregnant women who came to our hospital this morning. She arrived in severe pain, crying loudly, holding her back and abdomen because of the pain.
After about eight to ten minutes of bringing her into the labour ward, we examined her and found that the baby was already descending and her cervix was fully dilated.
Very shortly afterward, she delivered a baby girl.
So we carried out all the necessary and appropriate post-delivery care.
Not long after, we moved the mother and baby into a room so they could rest.
A little while later, the mother called us and said she was feeling very weak, tired, and that her eyes seemed dim or blurry. She also tried to eat after delivery but struggled to do so, and the food was not going down well.
She continued to feel weak, and she was also feeling dizzy.
What could have happened? Could it be that she lost a lot of blood and now needs a blood transfusion, or what should be done for her? Should we give her blood, or should we give her food?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Sàdédé ni a rí ìkan lára àwọn olóyún wa tí ó wá sí ilé ìwòsàn wa ní òwúrọ̀ yìí. Olóyún náà dé tìrora tìrora, tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní ké gidigidi, tó fi ọwọ́ di ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ mú, tó ń fi ọwọ́ di inú mú. Bẹ́ẹ̀ ló ń bẹ̀rẹ̀.

Kò pẹ́, a bá ìyá àti ọmọ gbé wọ inú yàrá lọ láti lọ sùn kí wọ́n lè fi wá dáradára.
Kò pẹ́ mọ́ ni ìyá ọmọ yìí pè wá pé òun máa ń sa rí i pé ó rẹ̀ òun wá, ó máa ń rẹ̀ òun wá, tí ojú òun sì ń ṣú. Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni arábìnrin yìí dé ń gbìyànjú láti jẹun nígbà tí a bímọ. Ó sá ń japitira láti jẹun nígbà tó bímọ tán, ṣùgbọ́n oúnjẹ yẹn ò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ lẹ́nu rẹ̀ dáadáa.

{"text": "Doctor, I brought my 5 years and 2 months old child, who has had this condition for about two months, who finds it difficult to breathe at night and also coughs all the time.
This cough has become persistent.
I bought a TB cough medicine called Tutolin Children for him; he has finished one bottle, but the cough has not gone, and it is still difficult for him to breathe at night.
I did a TB test for him, but they told me that he does not have tuberculosis.

Mo ṣe àyẹ̀wò ìkọ́ ìfẹ́ fún un, ṣùgbọ́n wọ́n jẹ́ kí n mọ̀ pé kò ní ìkọ́ ìfẹ́.
Nítorí náà dókítà, kí ni ó lè fà kí ọmọ ọdún márùn-ún máa wù ìkọ́ lẹ́mọ̀ lẹ́mọ̀, àti kí ni ó lè fà kí ọmọ ọdún márùn-ún nira fún láti mí tí ó bá ti di ní alẹ́?", "translated_text_language": "Yoruba", "audio_language": "Yoruba", "text_was_edited": false}

{"text": "\u200bA 22-year-old lady who gave birth at our hospital three days ago brought her baby today for routine immunizations. {"text": "Alabukun said that she has been having blurred vision, together with weakness, and that headache has not allowed her to be comfortable. {"text": "My daughter is pregnant; she is about twenty-four years old. She is the one who is pregnant. This happened today.

We took her to the hospital, and they examined her. They said the cervix has started to open a little, and that it is almost time for delivery.
Until today, the cervix is still opening until the time the baby will come out. Yesterday, the baby was still in pain that kept increasing since we arrived there.
She is in pain, the baby will come out, it is her first pregnancy. I am worried and my heart is troubled.
I want to save my child, and I do not want to lose the baby that is coming. Please, what could be causing this pain? Nígbà tí ó di alẹ́, mo ṣàkíyèsí pé ọmọ náà bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í ní ìrora. Ó sì ti kó ẹrù rẹ̀, ó ti wá sí ilé mi. Bí ìrora ṣe ń lọ, mo rí i pé ó ń pọ̀ sí i. Mo kó gbogbo ẹrù rẹ̀ jọ, kò sì jẹ́ kí a lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀.
A gbé e dé ilé ìwòsàn, wọ́n sì ṣàyẹ̀wò rẹ̀. Wọ́n sọ pé ilé-ọmọ ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í ṣí díẹ̀, àti pé kù díẹ̀ ni yóò tó ìgbà ìbímọ.
Ní òní ṣáájú, ilé-ọmọ ṣi ń ṣí sí i títí dé ìgbà tí ọmọ yóò fi bọ̀. Nígbà tí ó di ana, ọmọ náà wà nínú ìrora tí ó ń túbọ̀ ń pọ̀ sí i láti ìgbà tí a dé ibẹ̀.

{"text": "An elderly man came to our local hospital. This man said he has a severe headache, his neck is stiff, and he has rashes suddenly appearing on his body. He came to ask what could be causing it and what kind of treatment can be given to him.
We asked the man whether the headache started suddenly or if it came gradually. The man said it started suddenly at night and has become very severe now. We also asked him if he can look at light properly, and he said no, because light affects his head and makes the headache worse.
We also asked him about the rash on his body, whether it is painful, much, or mild. The man said it is all over his body, and he cannot point to one particular place, but it itches him.
After that, we asked him if he had contact with any sick person recently, and the man said they had not gone anywhere except selling goods in front of their house. They have not had contact with any sick person.
Our question for the doctor is what could cause this kind of headache and stiff neck where this man cannot turn his neck, with rashes all over his body? What can cause it? Is it an infectious disease or something else?
Our second question is what kind of tests can this man do to know exactly what is wrong with him for proper treatment, and what medicine can he use before his test results come out?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Bàbá àgbàlagbà kan ni wọ́n wá sí ilé ìwòsàn alábòde wa. Bàbá yìí sọ pé orí ń fò ó gan-an, ọrùn rẹ̀ sì le, ó sì ní kokoro kan ní ojijì tí ó sú sí i ní ara. Ó wá láti béèrè ohun tí ó lè fà á àti irú ìtọ́jú wo ni a lè fún un.
A béèrè lọ́wọ́ bàbá yìí pé ṣé orí náà bẹ̀rẹ̀ lójijì ni tàbí pé ó ti ń fò ó díẹ̀díẹ̀. Bàbá náà sì sọ pé lójijì ni ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní òru, ó sì ti lágbára gan-an báyìí. A tún béèrè lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀ pé ṣé ó lè wo ìmọ́lẹ̀ dáadáa, bàbá náà sì sọ pé rárá, kò lè wo ìmọ́lẹ̀ nítorí pé ó máa ń wọ agbárí rẹ̀, tí orí náà sì tún máa ń fò ó sí i.
A tún béèrè lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀ pé kokoro tí ó ń mú un yìí, ṣé ó ń le tàbí ó pọ̀, tàbí pé ó fẹ́rẹ̀fẹ́ ni. Bàbá náà sọ pé gbogbo ara òun ni, kò sì lè mọ ibi pàtó, ṣùgbọ́n ó ń yún un.
Lẹ́yìn náà, a béèrè lọ́wọ́ bàbá náà pé ṣé ó ní ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú aláìsàn kankan láìpẹ́ yìí, bàbá náà sì sọ pé wọn kò lọ sí ibi kankan ju pé wọ́n tà ọjà ní iwájú ilé wọn. Wọ́n kò sì ní ìfarakànra pẹ̀lú aláìsàn kankan.

{"text": "A woman noticed that her husband coughs very strongly when they wake up in the morning while still on the bed. The cough starts suddenly and takes a long time before it stops. As time goes on, she also notices that her husband struggles to breathe properly. When he walks a little distance or climbs stairs, he stops to catch his breath and becomes tired very quickly.
One day, after her husband spent a long time coughing and trying to regain his breath, the wife became worried. She started thinking that maybe there is a disease causing all these problems. The next day, she spoke with her husband to go to the hospital so that they can see a doctor and know exactly what is happening.
The question is what can cause a cough to be this severe, with constant tiredness and difficulty breathing all the time when the cough occurs? Can this problem be related only to lung disease or heart disease? What are the things that can cause death or make a person struggle to breathe severely, to the point that the person needs urgent medical attention?
What are the danger signs of breathing problems that the family should watch out for regarding cough and difficulty in breathing?", "text_language": "English", "translated_text": "Ìyàwó kan rí i pé ọkọ rẹ̀ ń wúkọ́ gan-an nígbà tí wọ́n bá jí ní orí ibùsùn. Ikọ́ náà máa ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ lójijì, ó sì máa ń gba àkókò kí ó tó dáwọ́ dúró. Bí ọjọ́ ṣe ń lọ, ó tún ń rí i pé ọkọ rẹ̀ ń tiraka láti mí dáadáa. Nígbà tí ó bá rìn jìnnà díẹ̀ tàbí gùn àtẹ̀gùn, ó máa ń dúró láti gba ẹ̀mí rẹ̀ padà, ó tún máa ń rẹ̀ kíákíá.
Ní ọjọ́ kan, lẹ́yìn tí ọkọ rẹ̀ gba àkókò pípẹ́ láti wúkọ́ àti láti gba ẹ̀mí rẹ̀ padà, inú ìyàwó náà bàjẹ́. Ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í rò pé bóyá àrùn kan wà tí ń fa gbogbo àwọn nǹkan wọ̀nyí. Ní ọjọ́ kejì, ó bá ọkọ rẹ̀ sọ̀rọ̀ pé kí wọ́n lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn, kí wọ́n lè rí dókítà, kí wọ́n lè mọ ohun tí ń ṣẹlẹ̀ gan-an.

Kí ni àwọn àmi ewu mímí tí ìdílé gbọ́dọ̀ máa ṣọ́ra fún nípa ikọ́ àti ìṣòro mímí?", "translated_text_language": "Yoruba", "audio_language": "Yoruba", "text_was_edited": false}

{"text": "\u200bWe saw one of our pregnant women early this morning along with her husband, she said that she has severe pain in her abdomen and her back is also aching, even though it is not yet up to her delivery date.
